name: 2.L Does the WWS use encryption to maintain the confidentiality of stored sensitive data?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.L: Does the WWS use encryption to maintain the confidentiality of stored sensitive data?

Recommendation (EPA): Do not store sensitive data, including credentials (i.e., usernames and passwords) in plain text files.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 3.K Utilize Strong Encryption (Protect). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Encryption of stored sensitive data.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 2.L Secure Sensitive Data. Outcome: Protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.. Risk addressed: Unsecured Credentials (T1552)
Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets (T1558)
OS Credential Dumping (T1003)
Data from Information Repositories (ICS T0811)
Theft of Operational Information (T0882). Scope: All passwords, credentials, secrets, and other sensitive or controlled information. NIST CSF: PR.DS-1, PR.DS-2, PR.DS-5. cost $$, impact High, complexity Medium.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/use-encryption.pdf

name: 2.I Does the WWS provide/conduct annual cybersecurity awareness training for all WWS personnel that covers basic cybersecurity concepts?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.I (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS provide/conduct annual cybersecurity awareness training for all WWS personnel that covers basic cybersecurity concepts?

Recommendation (EPA): Conduct cybersecurity awareness training annually, at a minimum, to help all employees understand the importance of cybersecurity and how to prevent and respond to cyberattacks.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 3.J Implement Cybersecurity Training (Protect). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Annual cybersecurity awareness training.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 2.I Basic Cybersecurity Training. Outcome: Organizational users learn and perform more secure behaviors. Risk addressed: User Training (M1017, ICS M0917). Scope: All employees and contractors. NIST CSF: PR.AT-1. cost $, impact High, complexity Low.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/provide-at-least.pdf

Source: EPA Water Cybersecurity Assessment Tool 3.1 (public domain); CISA CPG 1.0.1 component listing (public domain); crosswalk to CISA CPG 2.0 by BomberJacket Networks.

name: 1.D Does the WWS provide regular opportunities to strengthen communication and coordination between OT and IT personnel, including vendors?
description:
EPA checklist question 1.D: Does the WWS provide regular opportunities to strengthen communication and coordination between OT and IT personnel, including vendors?

Recommendation (EPA): Facilitate meetings between OT and IT personnel to provide opportunities for all parties to better understand organizational security needs and to strengthen working relationships.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 1.A Establish Cybersecurity Responsibilities (Govern); also 1.B Manage Cybersecurity Oversight. The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: IT and OT coordination is part of CPG 2.0 1.A's OT guidance.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 1.D Improving IT and OT Cybersecurity Relationships. Outcome: Improve OT cybersecurity and more rapidly and effectively respond to OT cyber incidents.. Risk addressed: Poor working relationships and mutual understanding between IT and OT cybersecurity can often result in increased risk for OT cybersecurity.. Scope: All IT and OT security personnel. NIST CSF: ID.GV-2. cost $, impact Medium, complexity Low.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/provide-regular-opportunities.pdf

Source: EPA Water Cybersecurity Assessment Tool 3.1 (public domain); CISA CPG 1.0.1 component listing (public domain); crosswalk to CISA CPG 2.0 by BomberJacket Networks.

name: 2.W Does the WWS ensure that assets connected to the public Internet expose no unnecessary exploitable services (e.g., remote desktop protocol)?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.W (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS ensure that assets connected to the public Internet expose no unnecessary exploitable services (e.g., remote desktop protocol)?

Recommendation (EPA): Eliminate unnecessary exposed ports and services on public-facing assets and regularly review.

External Remote Services (T1133, ICS T0822)

name: 1.C Does the WWS have a named role/position/title that is responsible for planning, resourcing, and executing OT-specific cybersecurity activities?

name: 1.E Does the WWS patch or otherwise mitigate known vulnerabilities within the recommended timeframe?
description:
EPA checklist question 1.E (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS patch or otherwise mitigate known vulnerabilities within the recommended timeframe?

Recommendation (EPA): Identify and patch vulnerabilities in a risk-informed manner (e.g., critical assets first) as quickly as possible.

Exploitation of Remote Service (T1210, ICS T0866)

External Remote Services (T1133, ICS T0822). Scope: Internet-facing assets. NIST CSF: ID.RA-1, PR.IP-12, DE.CM-8, RS.MI-3, ID.RA-6, RS.AN-5. cost $, impact High, complexity Medium.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/patch-or-otherwise.pdf

name: 2.J Does the WWS offer OT-specific cybersecurity training on at least an annual basis to personnel who use OT as part of their regular duties?

name: 2.M Does the WWS use email security controls to reduce common email-based threats, such as spoofing, phishing, and interception?

name: 2.S Does the WWS have a written cybersecurity incident response (IR) plan for critical threat scenarios (e.g., disabled or manipulated process control systems, the loss or theft of operational or fin…
description:
EPA checklist question 2.S (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS have a written cybersecurity incident response (IR) plan for critical threat scenarios (e.g., disabled or manipulated process control systems, the loss or theft of operational or financial data, exposure of sensitive information), which is regularly practiced and updated?

NIST CSF: PR.IP-9, PR.IP-10. cost $, impact High, complexity Low.

name: 2.Q Does the WWS require approval before new software is installed or deployed?

name: 2.H Does the WWS require multi-factor authentication (MFA) wherever possible, but at a minimum to remotely access WWS Operational Technology (OT)/Information Technology (IT) networks?

EPA checklist question 2.H (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS require multi-factor authentication (MFA) wherever possible, but at a minimum to remotely access WWS Operational Technology (OT)/Information Technology (IT) networks?

Recommendation (EPA): Deploy MFA as widely as possible for both operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT) networks. At a minimum, MFA should be used for remote access to the OT network.

name: 2.K Does the WWS use effective encryption to maintain the confidentiality of data in transit?

name: 1.I Does the WWS include cybersecurity as an evaluation criterion for the procurement of OT and IT assets and services?
description:

Recommendation (EPA): Include cybersecurity as an evaluation criterion when procuring assets and services. Where feasible, seek out systems that are secure by design and secure by default.

name: 4.A Does the WWS have a written procedure for reporting cybersecurity incidents, including how (e.g., phone call, Internet submission) and to whom (e.g., FBI or other law enforcement, CISA, state reg…
description:
EPA checklist question 4.A: Does the WWS have a written procedure for reporting cybersecurity incidents, including how (e.g., phone call, Internet submission) and to whom (e.g., FBI or other law enforcement, CISA, state regulators, WaterISAC, cyber insurance provider)?*

Under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022 (CIRCIA), CISA is required to issue regulations, through notice-and-comment rulemaking, requiring covered entities to report covered cyber incidents and ransom payments made as a result of a ransomware attack to CISA. CISA’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking proposes applying these requirements to at least some entities in the Water and Wastewater Sector. This recommendation will be revised as necessary when the CIRCIA Final Rule is issued.

Recommendation (EPA): Document the procedure for reporting cybersecurity incidents to better aid law enforcement, receive assistance with response and recovery, and to promote water sector awareness of cybersecurity threats.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 5.B Establish Incident Reporting Procedures (Respond). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Written incident reporting procedure.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 4.A Incident Reporting. Outcome: CISA and other organizations are better able to provide assistance or understand the broader scope of a cyberattack.. Risk addressed: Without timely incident reporting, CISA and other groups are less able to assist affected organizations and lack critical insight into the broader threat landscape (such as whether a broader attack is occurring against a specific sector).. Scope: Organization-wide. NIST CSF: RS.CO-2, RS.CO-4. cost $, impact High, complexity Low.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/have-a-written-procedure.pdf

Source: EPA Water Cybersecurity Assessment Tool 3.1 (public domain); CISA CPG 1.0.1 component listing (public domain); crosswalk to CISA CPG 2.0 by BomberJacket Networks.

name: 2.G Does the WWS detect and block repeated unsuccessful login attempts?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.G: Does the WWS detect and block repeated unsuccessful login attempts?

Recommendation (EPA): Enable System Administrator notification after a specific number of consecutive, unsuccessful login attempts in a short amount of time. At that point, future login attempts by the suspicious account should be blocked for a specified time or until re-enabled by an Administrator.

Brute Force - Password Spraying (T1110.003)

name: 2.F Does the WWS segment OT and IT networks and deny connections to the OT network by default unless explicitly allowed (e.g., by IP address and port)?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.F: Does the WWS segment OT and IT networks and deny connections to the OT network by default unless explicitly allowed (e.g., by IP address and port)?

Recommendation (EPA): Require connections between the OT and IT networks to pass through an intermediary, such as a firewall, bastion host, jump box, or demilitarized zone, which is monitored and logged.

Trusted Relationship (T1199)

Network Sniffing (T1040, ICS T0842). Scope: IT and OT assets, where safe and technically capable. NIST CSF: PR.AC-5, PR.PT-4, DE.CM-1. cost $$$, impact High, complexity High.

name: 2.E Does the WWS separate user and privileged (e.g., System Administrator) accounts?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.E (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS separate user and privileged (e.g., System Administrator) accounts?

Recommendation (EPA): Restrict System Administrator privileges to separate user accounts for administrative actions only and evaluate administrative privileges on a recurring basis to ensure accurate information for the individuals who have these privileges.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 3.G Administrators Maintain Separate User And Privileged Accounts (Protect). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Separate user and privileged accounts.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 2.E Separating User and Privileged Accounts. Outcome: Make it harder for threat actors to gain access to administrator or privileged accounts, even if common user accounts are compromised.. Risk addressed: Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859). Scope: IT and OT assets, where safe and technically capable. NIST CSF: PR.AC-4. cost $, impact High, complexity Low.

name: 2.C Does the WWS require unique and separate credentials for users to access OT and IT networks?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.C (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS require unique and separate credentials for users to access OT and IT networks?

Recommendation (EPA): Require a single user to have two different usernames and passwords; one account to access the IT network, and the other account to access the OT network to reduce the risk of an attacker being able to move between both networks using a single login.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 3.C Create Unique Credentials (Protect). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Unique credentials for OT and IT access.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 2.C Unique Credentials. Outcome: Attackers are unable to reuse compromised credentials to move laterally across the organization, particularly between IT and OT networks.. Risk addressed: Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)
Brute Force - Password Guessing (T1110.001). Scope: IT and OT assets. NIST CSF: PR.AC-1. cost $$, impact Medium, complexity Medium.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/require-unique.pdf

name: 1.B Does the WWS have a named role/position/title that is responsible for planning, resourcing, and executing cybersecurity activities within the WWS?
description:

Recommendation (EPA): Identify one role/position/title responsible for cybersecurity within the WWS. Whoever fills this role/position/title is then in charge of all WWS cybersecurity activities.

name: 2.D Does the WWS immediately disable access to an account or network when access is no longer required due to retirement, change of role, termination, or other factors?
description:
EPA checklist question 2.D (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS immediately disable access to an account or network when access is no longer required due to retirement, change of role, termination, or other factors?

Recommendation (EPA): Terminate access immediately to accounts or networks upon a change in an individual’s status making access unnecessary (i.e., retirement, change in position, etc.).

name: 2.R Does the WWS backup systems necessary for operations (e.g., network configurations, PLC logic, engineering drawings, personnel records) on a regular schedule, store backups separately from the so…
description:
EPA checklist question 2.R (EPA priority cybersecurity practice): Does the WWS backup systems necessary for operations (e.g., network configurations, PLC logic, engineering drawings, personnel records) on a regular schedule, store backups separately from the source systems, and test backups on a regular basis?

Recommendation (EPA): Regularly backup OT/IT systems so you can recover to a known and safe state in the event of a compromise. Test backup procedures and isolate backups from network connections. Implement the NIST 3-2-1 rule: 
3) Keep three copies: one primary and two backups; 
2) Keep the backups on two different media types; 
1) Store one copy offsite.

CISA CPG 2.0 goal: 3.O Maintain System Backups & Restoration Ability (Protect). The control and its evidence task are shared with the CPG 2.0 framework, so evidence collected once counts for both. Crosswalk note: Backups of systems necessary for operations.

CPG 1.0.1 practice 2.R System Backups. Outcome: Organizations reduce the likelihood and duration of data loss at loss of service delivery or operations.. Risk addressed: Data Destruction (T1485, ICS T0809)
Data Encrypted for Impact (T1486)
Disk Wipe (T1561)
Inhibit System Recovery (T1490)
Denial of Control (ICS T0813)
Denial/Loss of View (ICS T0815, T0829)
Loss of Availability (T0826)
Loss/Manipulation of Control (T0828, T0831). Scope: IT and OT assets necessary for business operations. NIST CSF: PR.IP-4. cost $$, impact High, complexity Medium.

EPA fact sheet: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-07/backup-systems-necessary_0.pdf

name: 2.P Does the WWS maintain updated documentation describing network topology (i.e., connections between all network components) across WWS OT and IT networks?

name: 3.A Does the WWS keep a list of threats and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for cyberattacks relevant to the WWS?

name: 2.V Does the WWS prohibit the connection of unauthorized hardware (e.g., USB devices, removable media, laptops brought in by others) to OT and IT assets?

name: 2.A Does the WWS change default passwords?
description:
